x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: lithium, nickel and cobalt (with manganese) usually make the cathode, while graphite is the anode. Statement 3 is wrong because only three of the four make the cathode, not graphite (the UPSC 2025 'only three' trap).

Compressed air storage does compress air into caverns and later expand it through turbines. The other pairs are swapped: rotational kinetic energy describes a flywheel, not pumped storage; pumping water uphill is pumped storage, not a flywheel; and converting hydrogen to electricity on board is a fuel-cell vehicle, not molten-salt storage, which stores heat in concentrated solar plants.

CCTS is administered by BEE, regulated by CERC and has a compliance mechanism using Carbon Credit Certificates, so B, C and D are features. It does not replace every PAT sector: as CCTS covers 9 heavy industries, PAT keeps four sectors (thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings).
